feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: Trump administration says it's scaling back fuel efficiency standards for new cars
entry.summary: The Trump administration is weakening Biden-era fuel efficiency standards for new cars and trucks.

entry.title: Pete Buttigieg discusses Trump administration's rollback of fuel efficiency standards
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg about the Trump administration's rollback of automotive fuel efficiency standards.

entry.title: News organizations ask court to bar White House enforcement of access ban
entry.summary: Three news outlets that President Trump banished from White House grounds asked a federal court to block the ban until the case is resolved.

entry.title: The Senate passes the Protect College Sports Act, but the bill's future is unclear
entry.summary: The bill's supporters, which include the NCAA, say it will tame what they call a "Wild West" era of college sports as litigation chips away at long-held rules around eligibility, transfers and pay.

entry.title: Could a far left candidate win a midterm race in a red state like Florida?
entry.summary: Angie Nixon, the Democratic U.S. Senate Candidate in Florida, is running from the far left — raising questions about whether such a campaign can work in a red state like Florida.

entry.title: Trump aims to leave a physical legacy in D.C., bulldozing norms along the way
entry.summary: President Trump has brought his New York real estate background to the White House. But experts say D.C. is a very different historic and legal landscape — and worry about the precedent he could set.

entry.title: What to know about the $810 million in spending canceled by President Trump
entry.summary: President Trump announced plans to cancel $810 million in congressionally approved spending, a move that some in his own party are calling illegal.

entry.title: Taxpayer-funded Trump administration ads raise questions about their legality
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former White House ethics czar Norman Eisen about the ethical and legal questions raised by new Trump administration advertisements, which are funded by taxpayer money.

entry.title: As Congress debates college sports, athletes-turned-senators have a seat at the table
entry.summary: The Protect College Sports Act is on the brink of passing in the Senate, where a handful of former college athletes who are now senators on both sides of the aisle have an extra say in the debate.

entry.title: Ohio governor's race: Ramaswamy and Acton clash in rare Democratic pickup opportunity
entry.summary: The Ohio governor's race pits former presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy against Democrat Amy Acton, a former state health advisor. Democrats see a chance to win a state that usually votes Republican.
